previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of recurrent lower extremity cellulitis, chronic venous insufficiency, bioprosthetic aortic valve, and pacemaker was admitted for worsening bilateral leg erythema, swelling, and pain, initially concerning for cellulitis. She had recently been diagnosed with C. difficile colitis and was on oral vancomycin. IV vancomycin was started in the ED but discontinued after evaluation by dermatology and infectious disease, who determined the leg changes were due to acute-on-chronic stasis dermatitis and lipodermatosclerosis rather than infection. She was treated with topical clobetasol, reduced-dose torsemide, IV fluids for dehydration, and continued oral vancomycin for C. diff. Her symptoms improved, and she was discharged home with home health nursing for wound care, instructions to complete her antibiotic course, and follow-up with her primary care physician.
